newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST - HK newspaper headlines - July 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - HK newspaper headlines - July 18.

text.p: These are some leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- MING PAO -- Hong Kong's Securities and Futures Commission would consider tightening its mortgage policy, if the number of mortgages handled by local banks continued to grow, in the hope of controlling property prices.

-- APPLE DAILY -- Because of the restraint shown by the Democratic Party during the handover, its chilly relationship with Beijing has begun to thaw slightly. Some Democrats could get back their home-visit permits -- the documents used by Hong Kong residents to go to China -- which were revoked by Beijing.

-- TA KUNG PAO -- Several experts speaking at a seminar said the Basic Law -- Hong Kong's post-handover constitution -- represented the spirit of tolerance, allowing people with different beliefs to co-exist.

-- ECONOMIC JOURNAL -- China Resources planned to set up a nationwide retail network and develop the healthcare products market. Managing director Ning Gaoning said the company would actively increase its land bank.

-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- Legal experts said Hong Kong's Court of Final Appeal should not be forced to refer the legal battle over residency for mainland-born children to the Chinese legislature, but should come to a decision on the matter by itself.
-- Drug workers accused local designer William Tang of promoting "heroin chic" after he sent his models down the catwalk at a fashion show with syringes sticking out of their clothes.
-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- A mainland official indicated Hong Kong media might be allowed to set up offices in Beijing.
